claims.text: At stage-1 DonHang.Api signed tokens (JwtTokenService, HMAC-SHA256) and validated them (SymmetricSecurityKey) with the same Jwt:SigningKey, so whatever can check a token can also create one.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.Api/Program.cs:22-43, JwtTokenService.cs; RFC 7518 §3.2 (HMAC with SHA-2, shared secret)

claims.text: Keycloak signs the realm's access tokens with an asymmetric key (RS256): the private key signs and stays in Keycloak; the matching public key verifies the signature but cannot produce one.
claims.source_hint: RFC 7518 §3.3 (RS256, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5); token header alg RS256 (outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/oauth-code-flow.txt 'eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs'); Keycloak Server Admin Guide: Realm keys

claims.text: Keycloak publishes a metadata document per realm at <realm>/.well-known/openid-configuration with issuer and jwks_uri; jwks_uri lists the realm's public keys, including one with use sig and alg RS256.
claims.source_hint: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 §3, §4 (issuer, jwks_uri); Keycloak docs; checked on running stage-2: /realms/donhang/protocol/openid-connect/certs

claims.text: AddJwtBearer downloads the metadata (MetadataAddress, or Authority + /.well-known/openid-configuration) and the public keys it points to, keeps them in memory, and fetches them again only now and then, never per request.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: configure JWT bearer authentication (Authority, MetadataAddress); JwtBearerOptions.ConfigurationManager / OpenIdConnect ConfigurationManager caching

claims.text: JwtBearer validates each token locally: signature with the cached public key, issuer, audience (donhang-api), lifetime; a failure gives 401 on an endpoint that requires an authenticated caller ([Authorize]).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: configure JWT bearer authentication; TokenValidationParameters defaults (ValidateIssuer, ValidateAudience, ValidateLifetime, ValidateIssuerSigningKey); Program.cs:37-39 comment

claims.text: Changing any claim of a signed JWT invalidates its signature, so the check fails.

compose sets Keycloak__Authority to the localhost:8180 realm (tokens' iss) and Keycloak__MetadataAddress to keycloak:8080/...; in the api container localhost is the api; the metadata fetched via keycloak:8080 still names the localhost:8180 issuer (KC_HOSTNAME).
RequireHttpsMetadata = false allows the metadata to be fetched over plain HTTP; by default JwtBearer requires HTTPS for the metadata address.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core API docs: JwtBearerOptions.RequireHttpsMetadata (default true); Program.cs:51

claims.text: The access token's sub is Keycloak's user id (UUID string, e.g. 92f6ba26-729c-4d61-854b-c04c9f2db11a for customer 1), not customers.id; at stage-1 OrdersController did int.Parse on sub.
CurrentCustomerAsync reads the sub claim from User and calls FindByIdentitySubjectAsync, which returns the customer whose identity_subject equals it, or null.
Migration AddCustomerIdentitySubject adds customers.identity_subject (nullable text) with a unique index and fills it for the five seeded customers by email.
POST /api/v1/orders answers 403 (Forbid) when the caller has no customer row, such as the staff account lan.do@example.com.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: OrdersController.cs:22-35; keycloak/donhang-realm.json (staff user); STAGE.md

claims.text: User in a controller holds the claims of the authenticated principal produced by the bearer token that passed validation; with MapInboundClaims = false the claim keeps the name sub.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: ControllerBase.User; JwtBearerOptions.MapInboundClaims; Program.cs:54

claims.text: Asking the authorization server about every token would add a call to every request and make every signed-in request fail while it is down; local validation avoids both.
claims.source_hint: reasoning from the design; RFC 7662 (introspection) not taught here

claims.text: With only local JwtBearer validation the API accepts a validly signed token until its exp (plus the default clock skew, 300 s, which Program.cs leaves unchanged); it cannot recall it earlier.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: JwtBearer validation (ValidateLifetime); RFC 7519 §4.1.4 exp; outline of backend.l2.refresh-tokens

claims.text: RS256 is the JWS algorithm name for RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256, a key-pair signature method, unlike HS256 (HMAC with SHA-256, one shared secret) used at stage-1.
